english: Let $p$ and $q$ be real numbers such that the parabolas $y=x^{2}$ and $y=2x^{2}+px+q$ intersect orthogonally at the point whose abscissa is $\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{4}$. Then the product of the slopes of the common tangents of these two parabolas is ______.
hindi: माना कि $p$ तथा $q$ ऐसी वास्तविक संख्याएँ हैं कि परवलय $y=x^{2}$ तथा $y=2x^{2}+px+q$ उस बिन्दु पर लम्बवत् प्रतिच्छेद करते हैं जिसका भुज $\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{4}$ है। तब इन दोनों परवलयों की उभयनिष्ठ स्पर्श रेखाओं की प्रवणताओं का गुणनफल ______ है।
solution: At $x_{0}=\frac{\sqrt2}{4}$ the slopes are $2x_{0}=\frac{\sqrt2}{2}$ and $4x_{0}+p=\sqrt2+p$; orthogonal: $\frac{\sqrt2}{2}(\sqrt2+p)=-1\Rightarrow p=-2\sqrt2$.
Tangent $y=2ax-a^{2}$ of $y=x^{2}$ touches the second parabola iff $2x^{2}+(p-2a)x+q+a^{2}=0$ has zero discriminant: $(p-2a)^{2}-8(q+a^{2})=0\Rightarrow 4a^{2}+4pa-p^{2}+8q=0$
solution_full: Let $x_{0}=\dfrac{\sqrt2}{4}$. The slope of $y=x^{2}$ at $x_{0}$ is $2x_{0}=\dfrac{\sqrt2}{2}$, and the slope of $y=2x^{2}+px+q$ is $4x_{0}+p=\sqrt2+p$.
The curves cut orthogonally, so the product of the slopes is $-1$: $\dfrac{\sqrt2}{2}(\sqrt2+p)=-1\Rightarrow 1+\dfrac{\sqrt2}{2}p=-1\Rightarrow p=-2\sqrt2$.
Every tangent of $y=x^{2}$ is $y=2ax-a^{2}$ for some $a$. It touches $y=2x^{2}+px+q$ iff $2x^{2}+(p-2a)x+(q+a^{2})=0$ has a repeated root: $(p-2a)^{2}-8(q+a^{2})=0$, i.e. $4a^{2}+4pa-p^{2}+8q=0$.
With $p=-2\sqrt2$, $q=\dfrac78$: $4a^{2}-8\sqrt2a-8+7=0$, i.e. $4a^{2}-8\sqrt2a-1=0$, whose discriminant $128+16>0$ gives two common tangents.
Their slopes are $2a_{1}$, $2a_{2}$ with $a_{1}a_{2}=-\dfrac14$, so the product of the slopes is $4a_{1}a_{2}=-1$ (the common tangents are perpendicular; explicitly the slopes are $2\sqrt2\pm3$).
originality_note: New: orthogonal intersection of two coaxial-direction parabolas fixes the second one, whose common tangents with the first turn out to be perpendicular (way 3: a family fixed by two conditions). Closest known: c for which y = x^2 and y = c - x^2 cut at right angles; common tangents of two parabolas. Different because: the parabolas open the same way, so they intersect and still have two common tangents, and the orthogonality fixes them.
blueprint_concepts: Angle of intersection between two curves and orthogonal curves

concept_use.Angle of intersection between two curves: Slopes sqrt2/2 and sqrt2 + p multiply to -1, giving p = -2 sqrt2.
concept_use.Common tangent/normal between two curves: Tangent y = 2ax - a^2 touching the second parabola gives 4a^2 - 8 sqrt2 a - 1 = 0 and the product of slopes -1.

Checked two common tangents exist (discriminant positive). No change.
key_step: Orthogonality and the common point fix p and q; tangency by discriminant gives a quadratic in a.
justification: A routine chain of standard steps (orthogonality, common point, discriminant tangency, Vieta) with surd arithmetic but no insight; L2 like the angle-between-tangents anchor 2026-P2-Q17.
